diagnostic_evidence.quote: Applying complementary slackness yields the characterization in Table~\ref{tab:kkt}.
The multiplier $\rho$ coincides with the bias $b$ of the primal model

issues.failure_explanation: With lambda_i and mu_i defined as the multipliers of u_i >= 0 and u_i <= C_{k(i)} (lambda_i u_i = 0, mu_i(u_i - C_{k(i)}) = 0) and rho the multiplier of s^T u = 0, stationarity is G_i + s_i rho = lambda_i - mu_i, i.e. G_i - s_i rho = lambda_i - mu_i under the convention b = tau_i = -rho used everywhere else. The displayed equation G_i - s_i rho = mu_i - lambda_i is the negative of this. Complementary slackness applied to the displayed equation gives tau_k = -rho + lambda_k >= -rho when alpha_k = 0, contradicting the table row tau_k <= -rho (and likewise every row of tab:kkt), so the stated inference 'Applying complementary slackness yields the characterization in Table' is invalid. The following remark is also self-contradictory, saying rho 'coincides with the bias b' and then that b = -rho.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed stationarity condition by G_i - s_i rho = lambda_i - mu_i (equivalently flip one side of the equation) so that complementary slackness yields tab:kkt, and state the convention as b = -rho in the following remark.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the KKT characterization is invalid as written and the printed stationarity condition contradicts the KKT table on which the working-set rules, the shrinking criteria and the bias recovery are built; the sign convention for rho is inconsistent between the equation, the table and the following remark. The table itself and all algorithmic claims are unaffected.
issues.title: KKT stationarity equation is the negative of the true condition and contradicts the KKT table
issues.why_classification: A one-line sign correction plus the matching sign statement restores the derivation and matches the already-correct KKT table, bias formulas and algorithm; no claim, regime or guarantee is lost and no new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Table tab:kkt gives tau_k <= -rho when alpha_k = 0 and tau_k = -rho when alpha_k is free, so tau_i <= -rho for every i in Iup (Iup consists of indices with alpha_k < C_k or alpha_k* > 0); dually tau_j >= -rho for every j in Idown. Hence at optimality tau_{i*} = max_{Iup} tau <= -rho <= min_{Idown} tau = tau_{j*}, the reverse of the displayed chain. Counterexample inside the regime the remark addresses: N = 2, y = (1,1), Omega = I, epsilon = 10 (so epsilon/100 = 0.1) and C = 0.01 (so C_k = 1). The objective is (1/2)||alpha - alpha*||^2 + 0.2*(sum of all variables' mass S) >= 0 with equality only at alpha = alpha* = 0, which is therefore the unique optimum; all four variables sit at their lower bounds and S_free is empty, tau = (0.9, 0.9, 1.1, 1.1), so tau_{i*} = 0.9 and tau_{j*} = 1.1 and KKT forces 0.9 <= -rho <= 1.1, while the displayed chain asserts 0.9 >= -rho >= 1.1, which is impossible. The same fixed ordering is asserted in the shrinking section ('the optimal threshold -rho lies in the interval [tau_{j*}, tau_{i*}]'), where it is valid only while Delta > 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the two inequalities to tau_{i*} <= -rho <= tau_{j*} and qualify the shrinking-section bracketing sentence by the sign of Delta; keep the midpoint estimator.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed bracketing of the multiplier (and hence of the bias) in the degenerate case with no free support vectors is false and contradicts the paper's own KKT table; the shrinking section's unconditional bracketing sentence is likewise false at a degenerate KKT point. The midpoint estimator (tau_{i*}+tau_{j*})/2, the shrinking criteria and the algorithm's output survive, since the midpoint is symmetric in tau_{i*} and tau_{j*}.
issues.title: Multiplier bound in the degenerate bias case is stated with reversed inequalities
issues.why_classification: Reversing two inequality signs in one display (plus a one-clause qualification of the shrinking sentence) restores a true statement while preserving the midpoint bias rule, the shrinking criteria and every guarantee; no new lemma, construction or reoptimization is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The only loop in Algorithm 1 is the For over t = 1,...,maxiter; the unshrinking branch 'Reset A <- {1,...,N}, F <- empty; continue outer loop' is placed after that loop has already terminated, so 'outer loop' does not exist and the instruction has no defined effect. When the branch is taken (maxiter exhausted with Delta^full > eps_tol, or a frozen variable still violating KKT after the post-loop check), the procedure neither re-enters the optimization nor returns, so the pseudocode is not a well-defined terminating procedure and cannot deliver the certification promised in the unshrinking paragraph.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Wrap the working-set loop in an outer loop that re-enters the iterations after each unshrinking reset (re-arming the iteration budget) and returns only when Delta^full <= eps_tol, reporting failure at a global iteration cap.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm's input-output contract and its eps_tol-optimality certification fail whenever shrinking has hidden a KKT violation or the iteration budget is exhausted; the finite-termination/convergence guarantee quoted in the computational remarks is unsupported for the printed procedure.
issues.title: Unshrinking branch of Algorithm 1 targets a nonexistent outer loop, so the algorithm cannot return a certified solution
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local restructuring of the control flow with an iteration cap; it restores the stated certification and preserves the method, the rates and the advertised scope, with no new lemma, construction or replacement argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: need not be positive semi-definite, so $\eta_s < 0$ is possible.
For the symmetric-kernel variant (m2) with $a = +1$, $P \succeq 0$ is preserved and the same guarantees apply.

issues.failure_explanation: Omega* with entries K(x_k, -x_l) is a cross-Gram matrix of the families {phi(x_k)} and {phi(-x_k)}, not a Gram matrix, and it need not be PSD: for the RBF kernel used elsewhere in the paper (gamma = 1) at x_1 = 1, x_2 = 2, Omega* = [[e^{-4}, e^{-9}],[e^{-9}, e^{-16}]] has determinant e^{-20} - e^{-18} < 0. The stated reason is therefore false, and the conclusion Omega_s >= 0 for a = +1 does not follow and can fail (a PSD kernel can be built whose feature map sends x_1, x_2, -x_1, -x_2 to e_1, e_2, (-1/2, 1), (1, -1/2), giving Omega_s = (1/2)[[1/2, 1],[1, 1/2]], which is indefinite). Conversely, for kernels with K(-x,-x') = K(x,x') (e.g. RBF), (Omega_s)_{kl} = <psi_a(x_k), psi_a(x_l)> with psi_a(x) = (phi(x) + a phi(-x))/2, so Omega_s is PSD for BOTH signs of a; the companion assertion that Omega_s may be indefinite for a = -1 (and hence that the convergence proof does not extend to a = -1) is thus also wrong for the kernels the paper uses.

failure_location.quote:
For $a = +1$ (even symmetry), $\Omega_s \succeq 0$
follows from the fact that $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the PSD claim by a correct statement: under K(-x,-x') = K(x,x') prove (Omega_s)_{kl} = <psi_a(x_k), psi_a(x_l)> with psi_a(x) = (phi(x) + a phi(-x))/2, hence Omega_s is PSD for both a = +1 and a = -1; note that without such a hypothesis on K neither Omega* nor Omega_s is guaranteed PSD and restrict the m2 guarantees accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The convexity of the m2 dual, the sufficiency of its KKT conditions and the convergence guarantee claimed for a = +1 (abstract, algorithm adaptation and computational remarks) are unsupported and can fail; at the same time the announced loss of those guarantees for a = -1 is unfounded for the kernels considered, so the stated scope of the m2 solver is wrong in both directions.
issues.title: PSD analysis of the symmetric kernel Omega_s rests on the false claim that Omega* is positive semi-definite
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a contained nontrivial argument (the symmetrized-feature-map lemma) and an added hypothesis on K; the solver, the curvature and gradient formulas and the m2 guarantees survive for the standard kernels (RBF and other even translation-invariant kernels), so the loss is a narrowing of the kernel class rather than a new proof architecture or an abandoned result.
